spans.s:
विंश a. (शी f.) Twentieth.
--शः
A twentieth part.

विंशतिः f. Twenty, a score.
--Comp.
--ईशः, --ईशिन् m. a ruler of twenty
villages.

विंशिन् m.
1 Twenty, a score.
--2
A lord or ruler of twenty villages.
विंजामरं The white of the eye.

.
--2 To roar, cry out.
--3
To fill with cries. --Caus. To cause
to cry or utter notes; अंबुदैः
शिखिगणो विनाद्यते Ghaṭ. 10.

1 Sound, noise.
--2 N. of a
tree.

विनम् {c1c} P. To bend oneself,
stoop, be bent; विनमंति चास्य तरवः
प्रचये

विनत p. p.
1 Bent down, bowed.
--2 Stooping, drooping, inclined;
Ś. 3. 10.
--3 Sunk down, depressed.
--4 Bent, crooked, curved.
--5
Humble, modest.
--6 Changed into a
lingual letter; see विनाम.
--Comp.
--आनन a. with downcast face,
dejected.

1 N. of the mother of
Aruṇa and Garuḍa, said to be one
of the wives of Kaśyapa; see गरुड.
--2 A kind of basket.
--Comp.
--नंदनः, --सुतः, --सूनुः epithets of
Garuḍa or Aruṇa.

विनतिः f.
1 Bowing down,
bending, stooping.
--2 Modesty,
humility.
--3 A request.

विनम्रकं The flower of the Tagara
tree.

To be destroyed,
perish, die.
--2 To disappear, vanish.
--3 To be lost or ruined.
--4 To be
frustrated or foiled. --Caus. To
destroy, annihilate.

विनशनं Perishing, loss,
destruction, disappearance.
--नः N. of the
place where the river Sarasvatī is
lost in the sand; cf.

विनाशनं Destruction, ruin,
annihilation.
--नः A destroyer.

विनष्ट p. p.
1 Perished,
destroyed, ruined.
--2 Disappeared, lost.
--3
Spoiled, corrupted.

विनष्टिः f.
1 Utter ruin or
destruction.
--2 Disappearance, vanishing.

1 Destruction, ruin, utter
loss, decay.
--2 Removal.
--Comp.
--उन्मुख a. about to perish, ripe to
meet one's doom.
--धर्मन्, --धर्मिन् a.
subject to decay, perishable,
transient; विषयेषु विनाशधर्मसु
त्रिदिवस्थेष्वपि निःस्पृहोऽभवत्

विना ind. Without, except (with
acc., instr. or abl.); यथा तानं विना
रागो यथा मानं विना नृपः । यथा दानं
विना हस्ती तथा ज्ञानं विना यतिः

; पंकैर्विना सरो भाति सदः
खलजनैर्विना । कटुवर्णैर्विना काव्यं मानसं
विषयैर्विना 1. 116; विना वाहनहस्तिभ्यः क्रियतां
सर्वमोक्षः

; Śi. 2. 9. (विनाकृ
means ‘to leave, abandon, bereave,
deprive of’; मदनेन विनाकृता रतिः

‘bereft of Cupid’).
--Comp.
--उक्तिः f. a figure of speech
in which विना is used in a poetically
charming way; विनार्थसंबंध एव
विनोक्तिः R. G.; see K.

विन्न p. p. [विद् कर्मणि क्त]
1
Known.
--2 Got, obtained.
--3
Discussed, investigated.
--4 Placed,
[]
fixed.
--5 Married; (See विद्).

विनाडिः, विनाडिका A measure
of time equal to one-sixtieth part
of a Ghaṭikā or equal to 24 seconds.

विनाडिः, विनाडिका A measure
of time equal to one-sixtieth part
of a Ghaṭikā or equal to 24 seconds.

विनामः (In gram.). Change
into a lingual or cerebral letter, the
substitution of ष् for स् and ण् for न्.

1 A remover (of
obstacles).
--2 N. of Gaṇeśa.
--3 A
Buddhist deified teacher.
--4 N. of
Garuḍa.
--5 An obstacle, impediment.

विनाहः A cover for the mouth
of a well; cf. वीनाह.

वीनाहः The top or cover of a
well.

विनिकीर्ण p. p. Scattered, thrown
about.

To entrust,
deliver over.
--2 To place in or upon.
--3 To throw down, overthrow.
--4
To engage in.

विनिगड a. Without fetters,

To restrain,
check; obstruct, impede.
--2 To lay
hold of, seize.

1 Sleepless, awake
[]

गुरुर्विनिद्रः

विनिपातितो यामि

.

.

--2

--2
To disappear, vanish.
--3 To go

--4 To escape from,

master.

--2

--3 A settled rule.

विनिर्मित p. p.
1 Formed or made

--2 Made, created.
--3

--4

To loosen, free
from.

.

विनिवार्य

.

1 N. of a range of
mountains which separates Hindustān
proper from the Deccan or south;
it is one of the seven Kulaparvatas
q. v., and forms the southern limit
of Madhyadeśa; see

.
[According to a legend, the Vindhya
mountain, being jealous of the mount
Meru (or Himālaya) demanded that
the sun should revolve round himself
as about Meru, which the sun declined
to do; whereupon the Vindhya began
to rise higher and higher so as to
obstruct the path of the sun and moon.
The gods being alarmed sought the aid
of the sage Agastya, who approached
the mountain and requested that by
bending down he would give him an
easy passage to the south, and that he
would retain the same position till his
return. This Vindhya consented to do
(because according to one account, he
regarded Agastya as his teacher); but
Agastya never returned from the south,
and Vindhya never attained the height
of Meru].
--2 A hunter.
